h1: Flight reservation for a Canada visa
lead: A clear itinerary for your Canadian visitor visa file, without paying for a ticket before a decision.
body: ## Travel plans in a Canada visitor application

Canadian visitor applications are mostly submitted online, so the quality and consistency of your uploaded documents matter. Official guidance focuses on your purpose, funds and ties to home, and it generally advises against buying non-refundable tickets before a decision. An itinerary can illustrate your plan, but it does not carry the application. Our [Canada visa itinerary guide](/blog/canada-visa-flight-itinerary) explains the detail.
## What you receive

- A flight reservation with a booking reference (PNR)
- Your name as on the passport
- Route, dates and flight numbers
- A PDF that uploads cleanly
See the [sample ticket](/sample-ticket).
## Where it helps

- Specific dates that match your application form
- Support for an invitation letter from a host in Canada
- A tidy plan for a trip with several stops
- An exit date that fits within the stay you request
## Where it does not
It does not prove funds or ties to home, and it does not satisfy a direct request for a paid ticket. If an office asks for a specific document, provide that document.
> A reservation is not a ticket and does not guarantee a visa. We cannot promise acceptance.
## Prepare your upload
Export or scan clearly, name files sensibly and keep dates consistent across documents. Do not edit the PDF. If your plan changes, order a new itinerary.
## Related pages

See the [US visa](/dummy-ticket-for-us-visa) and [UK visa](/dummy-ticket-for-uk-visa) pages if you apply elsewhere too. For a one-way document, see [onward ticket](/onward-ticket). Check [pricing](/pricing) for plans.
## Cover letters

A short letter of explanation can tie your documents together: who you are, the purpose of the trip, the dates, who is paying, where you will stay and why you will return. Refer to the documents in your file by name. Keep it factual and consistent with the form, because an officer will notice if a date or city differs.
## Family, business and group travel

If you are invited by someone in Canada, the invitation letter and your own documents should line up, and your file should still show why you will return. For a business visit, include the host's invitation and a letter from your employer. For children, check the guidance on consent letters. Our [visa application checklist](/blog/visa-application-checklist) lists the usual supporting documents.

Q: Is a flight itinerary required for a Canada visitor visa?
A: Official guidance generally treats it as optional supporting evidence unless you are asked for it. Check the current document list for your country.

Q: Can I upload the PDF as it arrives?
A: Yes. Keep it unedited and check that the names and dates match your form.
